title: Invariant symmetric-power lifting over an arbitrary ring
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $C$ a commutative Hopf $R$-algebra, with comultiplication $\Delta:C\to C\otimes_R C$, counit $\epsilon:C\to R$ and antipode, satisfying the Hopf identities. Tensor products are [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. For an arbitrary $R$-module $M$, a rational right coaction is an $R$-linear map $\rho:M\to M\otimes_R C$ with $(1\otimes\epsilon)\rho=1$ and $(\rho\otimes1)\rho=(1\otimes\Delta)\rho$, using the standard unit and associator identifications. The induced symmetric algebra coaction is the unique algebra map extending $(\iota_M\otimes1)\rho$ by [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-universal-property]. Use the degree-$n$ tensor-image submodule of [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-graded] for $\operatorname{Sym}^n_R M$. Define $P(R,C)$ to mean: for every such $M,\rho$, with no finiteness or flatness assumption, and every surjective $R$-linear $\lambda:M\to R$ satisfying $(\lambda\otimes1)\rho(m)=\lambda(m)\otimes1$, there exist $n>0$ and $q\in\operatorname{Sym}^n_R M$ with $\operatorname{Sym}(\rho)(q)=q\otimes1$ and $\widetilde\lambda(q)=1$, where $\widetilde\lambda:\operatorname{Sym}_R M\to R$ is the unique algebra map extending $\lambda$. In degree $n$ this is $\operatorname{Sym}^n(\lambda)$ under $\operatorname{Sym}^n_R R\simeq R$.

source.place: Lemma 9.2.5(5), p.522; Theorem 9.7.5 and preceding split-group convention, pp.526–527. Online original: https://content.algebraicgeometry.nl/2014-4/2014-4-022.pdf
